title: Migration idempotence keys on Quest durable status, not the local pending record (DEC-172 (4ap))
description: Ruled by opum-doc DEC-172 (4ap)/(4ap)(a) (opum-doc origin/dev). LCLI-699 round 2 found the residual: a rerun after an applied migration stayed idempotent only while the local pending record .lore/quest-backlog-migration.pending.json survived, and a migration that completes with no removal requested clears that record, so a later --remove-backlog rerun re-enters the fresh path and collides (exit 5). (4ap) keys idempotence on Quest durable status instead; (4ap)(a) uses a lore-side last-applied-digest hint confirmed by Quest for the divergence arm, with Quest alias-collision refusal as the backstop. Also absorbs the two LCLI-699 minors: the rollback remedy flags and the end-to-end repro.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A rerun of lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog, with or without --remove-backlog, runs at most ONE read-only preview to compute the current digest and then asks Quest migration backlog status --digest <digest>; the local pending record is a cache only, never the gate.

When Quest status shows the digest APPLIED, the run exits 0 with the existing receipt plus alreadyApplied: true and applies nothing; with --remove-backlog it then performs the verified archive, verify, remove.
When Quest holds no receipt for the digest, the run performs a genuinely fresh migration.

On a successful apply, lore records the LAST APPLIED migrationDigest as a hint in its own init state; on a rerun, a current digest that DIFFERS from a hint which status(hint) confirms applied refuses with the (4aj)(c) named divergence code backlog.diverged-from-migration, applying nothing. No hint, or an unconfirmed hint, is treated as FRESH; the hint is never the gate on its own, and Quest alias-collision refusal remains the backstop against a double apply.
The post-migration notice truthfully names --remove-backlog as the next step for a completed no-removal migration.
The rollback remedy names --actor and --actor-kind so quest migration backlog rollback runs as printed (the F4 nit from LCLI-699).
Tests: the LCLI-700 repro end to end (migrate without removal, pending cleared, rerun with --remove-backlog, exit 0, alreadyApplied, verified removal), and the existing (4aj) paths stay green.
